name: Mino AI
tagline: An AI assistant that generates short-form content hooks, angles and scripts for creators and marketers.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Strip away the chat avatar and this is a prompt, a system message, and a library of hook formulas sitting in front of a frontier model. The hard part of content ideation was never generating a hundred openers, it was knowing which ones actually landed for your specific audience, and no vendor has that for you either. A coding agent can build you a local hook generator with your own swipe file, your own niche context, and a scoring pass in an afternoon, and it will be more tailored than a generic one because you control the examples. The genuine asset a tool like this could hold is a scraped corpus of high-performing posts with real engagement numbers, and if that corpus is doing the work the output quality is hard to match from scratch. From the outside it is not clear that it is, which is why the honest answer is build it and compare.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you paste a topic plus your niche and audience, and it returns scored hook variants built from a formula library and your own swipe file of posts that worked.
requirements: An LLM API key, OpenAI or Anthropic, in .env
Node 20 and a local SQLite file
Twenty to fifty of your own hooks or competitor hooks to seed the swipe file
whatYouLose: Someone else's curated hook formula library, which is genuinely a head start if theirs is good
Any trend data about what is working on each platform this week
A polished chat UI and a persona that makes ideation feel like a conversation instead of a form
Mobile access, unless you deploy the thing somewhere
Whatever platform-specific formatting and length rules they have already tuned
moatNotes: The only defensible version of this product is a live corpus of posts with real performance numbers attached. A formula library is a PDF with a login.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because staring at a blank editor is a real problem and paying twenty dollars to never do it again is a rational trade. Most buyers of hook tools do not want a generator, they want a prompt they do not have to write and a list they can skim at 9am. A DIY build solves the generation but not the habit, and the vendor's formula library plus a friendly interface is doing more psychological work than technical work. That is a legitimate thing to sell, it is just not a thing that is hard to rebuild.
notes: The interesting question is whether there is a real performance corpus behind this or just a system prompt in a nice coat.
prompt:
Build a local-first content hook generator called "hookbench". Stack: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, and better-sqlite3. No auth, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud database. Everything runs on localhost against a single hooks.db file in the project root.

Data model, three tables:
- profiles: id, name, niche, audience_description, tone_notes, platform (tiktok, youtube_shorts, linkedin, x, instagram)
- swipe: id, profile_id, hook_text, source_url, platform, metric_note (freeform, e.g. "1.2M views"), tags
- generations: id, profile_id, topic, created_at, raw_json

Features, in scope:
1. A profiles page to create and edit profiles. Seed one example profile on first run.
2. A swipe file page: paste a hook, tag it, attach an optional metric note and source URL, list and filter by profile and platform.
3. A generate page: pick a profile, type a topic or raw idea, choose how many variants (default 12). On submit, call the LLM with a system prompt that includes the profile fields, a built-in library of hook patterns (curiosity gap, contrarian claim, specific number, before/after, direct callout, mistake confession, list promise, question hook), and up to 15 of that profile's swipe entries as style examples.
4. Ask the model to return strict JSON: an array of objects with hook, pattern_used, why_it_might_work, and a self_score from 1 to 10. Render as cards sorted by self_score descending. Validate the JSON with zod and retry once on parse failure.
5. Each card has buttons: copy, and "save to swipe" which writes it back into the swipe table so good output compounds.
6. A history page listing past generations with the topic and the top three hooks, clickable to reopen the full result.

Out of scope, do not build: scraping any platform, trend data, posting or scheduling, image generation, user accounts, payments, analytics dashboards.

LLM access: a single server-side route using the Anthropic SDK, model and key read from .env (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, MODEL). Never expose the key client-side. Commit .env.example, gitignore .env.

Ship a README with setup in four commands and one paragraph explaining that output quality tracks swipe file quality, so seed it before judging the thing.
